But ''Kh''ih Yû appears as a rebel, or opposed to the One man in all the country who was then fit to rule. It is difficult to imagine how they could be associated, and sacrificed to together.</ref>submission,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And throughout the region none had dared to insult him.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The engines of onfall and assault were (then) vigorously plied,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Against the walls of ''Kh''ung very strong.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He attacked it, and let loose all his forces;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He extinguished (its sacrifices)<ref>The extinction of its sacrifices was the final act in the extinction of a state. Any members of its ruling House who might survive could no longer sacrifice to their ancestors as having been men of princely dignity. The family was reduced to the ranks of the people.</ref>, and made an end of its existence;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And throughout the kingdom none dared to oppose him.

<section begin="ode9" />{{dhr}}
{{c|{{sc|Ode 9. The {{tooltip|Hsiâ Wû|Xià Wǔ}}.}}}}
{{dhr|0%}}
{{smaller block/s}}
{{hanging indent/s}}
{{asc|In praise of [[w:King Wu of Zhou|king Wû]], walking in the ways of his forefathers, and by his filial piety securing the throne to himself and his posterity.}}
{{hanging indent/e}}
{{smaller block/e}}

{{center block/s}}
Successors tread in the steps (of their predecessors) in our {{tooltip|''K''âu|Zhōu}}.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
For generations there had been wise kings;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The three sovereigns were in heaven<ref>'The three sovereigns,' or 'wise kings,' are to be understood of the three celebrated in [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shih/The Major Odes of the Kingdom/Decade 1/Ode 7|ode 7]],—[[w:King Tai of Zhou|Thâi]], [[w:Ji, King of Zhou|''K''î]], and [[w:King Wen of Zhou|Wăn]]. We are thus obliged, with all Chinese scholars, to understand this ode of [[w:King Wu of Zhou|king Wû]]. The statement that 'the three kings were in heaven' is very express.</ref>;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And king ({{tooltip|Wû|Wǔ}}) was their worthy successor in his capital<ref>The capital here is [[w:Haojing|Hâo]], to which [[w:King Wu of Zhou|Wû]] removed in {{BC}} 1134, the year after his father's death. It was on the east of the river [[w:zh:灃河 (渭河)|Făng]], and only about eight miles from [[w:King Wen of Zhou|Wăn]]'s capital of [[w:Fengjing (Zhou)|Făng]].</ref>.

King (Wû) was their worthy successor in his capital,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Rousing himself to seek for the hereditary virtue,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Always striving to be in accordance with the
